sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Expect gory set pieces and jump scares galore in the return of the supernatural anthology series, with Dan Stevens among the many poor souls terrorised by an evil spirit haunting their ward Things that go bump in the night? Bad. Things that go bump in the night in a dilapidated psychiatric hospital? Infinitely worse. That, basically, is the premise of Devil in Silver, the latest volume of anthology series The Terror, which began in 2018 with a supernaturally charged tale of a polar expedition to find out what happened to Sir John Franklin’s voyage. Crikey, it does not end well. The next was set during the second world war and was about shapeshifters from Japanese folklore terrorising a Japanese-American community in southern California. A hiatus followed, but now The Terror is back with a double dose of horror: a malevolent spirit moving in and out of the bodies of the patients of New Hyde psychiatric hospital, and the more tangible but no less frightening diabolism of the US mental healthcare system. Pepper (Dan Stevens, still of Downton Abbey fame despite his many varied roles since) is in New Hyde because the three policemen who arrested him after they caught a few punches he was aiming at his girlfriend’s controlling ex threw him in there rather than completing the paperwork the station would have required. There he meets the lost and suffering souls who have ended up in what amounts, due to underfunding and understaffing, to a holding pen rather than a rehabilitative or care facility. Dorry (Judith Light) is the longest-serving resident – put there decades ago by her husband because of her endless crying fits, though her later memories reveal a greater darkness. sources.summary: This Booker-listed epic set in Aids-era Kingston is a triumph – bitter, bawdy and ravishingly queer “A sense of sweep,” replied Marlon James, when asked what moves him most in literature. “Sweep isn’t just about external journeys, but internal as well. It can be over years and decades, or across land and sea.” If that explanation is still hazy, pick up his mighty new novel, which is longlisted for this year’s Booker prize and is tirelessly – sometimes exhaustingly – grand and peripatetic. Mounting a grisly exposé of Jamaican homophobia, this polyphonic 640-page doorstopper is an emotionally bruising narrative that roves “uptown, downtown, ghetto and gully” through Aids-era Kingston with sidetrack excursions to 1950s England and a closing leap to 2000s United States. The novel’s defining event is a gruesome mob attack on eight queer men who have clandestinely come together to work on bringing John Herbert’s 1967 gay prison play, Fortune and Men’s Eyes, to the stage. The goal, in the words of director Havelock Titus, is to shatter “the whole fragile myth of Jamaican male sexuality”. “Because prison,” he explains, “is the ultimate male institution and yet masculine sexualities that could never happen outside in the normal world flourish in there all the time.” Continue reading...

sources.summary: This portrait by Vytautas Katkus of a man contemplating his recent fatherhood and his own father is steeped in ennui and ends up drifting At one point in this Nordic-Baltic homecoming film, Danielius (Darius Šilėnas) refuses an invite for beachfront karaoke, preferring to watch from behind a polythene partition. At another, a neighbour glimpses him exercising across the courtyard, through the window of the flat in an end-of-summer Lithuanian resort that Danielius is trying to sell. Having returned from Norway to settle up accounts, this prodigal son is often holding the world at arm’s length – and director Vytautas Katkus does his best to help him with this distanced technique in this quizzical and faintly existential drama. Little tangible is disclosed. Danielius is a thirtysomething father who skipped the funeral of his own dad the year before. Preparing the flat to go on the market, he walks the dog of his neighbour, Vismante (Vismantė Ruzgaitė), hangs speculatively at beach gatherings and falls asleep in pine forests. Ice-cream is eaten at every available opportunity. He’s not alienated exactly, but somewhat out of step. As he looks for new anchorage, even the film seems to question whether Danielius has sufficient main character energy: it periodically drifts to follow another resident, Tomas (Rokas Siaurusaitis), who is caring for his grandmother over the way. items.headline: 本週藝文評論精選
items.context: 英國衛報這一輪藝文評論涵蓋範圍很廣——從愛丁堡藝穗節的深夜喜劇秀，到探討印度農村寡婦處境的紀錄片，再到逍遙音樂節上罕見的低音管協奏曲首演。三則評論風格迥異，但都指向創作者如何在各自領域裡處理沉重或荒謬的題材。
items.thread_text: 這幾天的藝文評論值得一看。愛丁堡藝穗節上，Ashley Blair與Drew Reilly的深夜喜劇秀《Fully Loaded》用誇張歌舞消化Z世代的存在焦慮；紀錄片《Marching in the Dark》記錄印度馬哈拉施特拉邦的農村寡婦，如何在丈夫因債務自殺後互相扶持撐過生活；而在皇家亞伯特音樂廳，98歲作曲家Thea Musgrave的低音管協奏曲《Out of the Darkness》迎來世界首演，由Amy Harman擔任獨奏。
items.threads_text: 這一輪藝文評論橫跨戲劇、紀錄片與古典音樂，題材落差很大，但都在處理沉重或荒謬的人生課題。愛丁堡藝穗節上，Brooklyn來的Ashley Blair與Drew Reilly端出深夜喜劇秀《Fully Loaded》，用歌舞把Z世代的存在焦慮唱成一場荒謬派對。紀錄片《Marching in the Dark》則把鏡頭對準印度馬哈拉施特拉邦——這裡是印度農民自殺率最高的地區之一，過去二十年已有超過 40 萬名農民輕生。片中記錄一群失去丈夫的寡婦，如何靠著彼此扶持撐過生活。另一頭，98歲的蘇格蘭作曲家Thea Musgrave在皇家亞伯特音樂廳迎來她的低音管協奏曲《Out of the Darkness》世界首演，由低音管手Amy Harman擔任獨奏，讓管弦樂團裡罕見的擔綱聲部，終於站上聚光燈下。

sources.summary: Underbelly, Cowgate, Edinburgh Ashley Blair and Drew Reilly send up gen Z anomie with hardcore ditties about awkward dinners, megachurches and centaur boyfriends ‘How to feel whole in an empty world?” There are many possible answers to that question, and Megasquirt’s late-night comedy rave workshops a good few of them. But there’s probably no better way than putting on a banging show and performing it to an adoring audience of your peers – and that’s what Brooklyn imports Ashley Blair and Drew Reilly do in Fully Loaded, turning the Underbelly at some ungodly hour into a pulsating queer(ish) celebration-cum-sendup of gen Z anomie. “Everything is empty / Life is a hole / You gotta fill it up,” they sing, looking like refugees from Warhol’s Factory but delivering comedy that couldn’t be more now. The show starts as if we’re being seconded to a generational revolution, but it’s soon clear that this pair, both Second City alumni, are threats to nothing but your funny bone. Their premise is that life is void of meaning. We flash back to meet them as alienated schoolkids and one terrific sketch, a silly symphony of clinking cutlery and ASMR tuts and sighs, imagines two parents at dinner, struggling to repress their mutual loathing. If this is our hosts’ generational inheritance, why not look for a better way of being? Like a romance with an inverted Centaur Boyfriend, the title of one daft ditty, or like forming a megachurch to start replenishing the spiritual chasm. Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Kinshuk Surjan’s documentary follows women in dire financial straits whose bereavement compounds their social plight, which they confront together Out in rural India, a crisis casts a dark cloud over the seemingly tranquil vistas of wheat fields and soy farms. Over the past 20 years, more than 400,000 farmers have killed themselves , beset by mounting debts and low market prices for crops. Shot in Maharashtra, the state with the highest rate of farmer suicides in India, Kinshuk Surjan’s documentary sensitively captures another tragedy that lingers after death: left behind by their dead husbands, generations of grieving widows struggle to find their way in a society still burdened by patriarchal values. Sanjivani, a woman in her 30s, is one such case. Eight years after her husband killed himself, she has taken over some of the farming responsibilities, along with other odd jobs, to provide for her two children. The camera rarely finds her at rest; Sanjivani not only works in the fields but also performs domestic labour for her extended family – cooking, cleaning and doing laundry. Her resilience is stunning to witness, but even more impressive is the emotional support provided by a tight-knit network of other widows. Together, the women gather for counselling sessions where they can freely discuss their emotional, physical and financial issues. Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Royal Albert Hall, London Amy Harman brought a warm baritonal vocalise to premiere from nonagenarian Thea Musgrave, while Felix Klieser bent his unique horn technique to Mozart Amid this year’s crop of Proms premieres, one stood out a mile – long before any of us had heard a note of it. Out of the Darkness is a new bassoon concerto by the 98-year-old Scottish composer Thea Musgrave , whose music was first heard at the Proms in 1960. Sixty-six years later, Musgrave is one of classical music’s most eminent elder stateswomen; her next opera will make its debut next year . But bassoon concertos remain a rare breed. The first performance of Out of the Darkness emerged from a dark grumble of the Academy of St Martin in the Fields’ percussion and bass instruments, which bassoonist Amy Harman answered from the back of the stage, weaving a warm, baritonal vocalise through the orchestral duskiness. Only the solo violin line of ASMF’s director Benjamin Marquise Gilmore offered a lighter, brighter sound, until it was picked up by the rest of the violins. The musical material was all beguiling loops and phrases ending in question marks, Harman’s tone deliciously lyrical. Nothing was spelled out, except her journey around the orchestra, the bassoon gathering rhythmic vitality as she walked to join the trumpets, then double basses, finally arriving at the front – a soloist’s standard spot – in time for the disarmingly near-tonal final chord. Continue reading...

items.context: Twitch與其母公司Amazon面臨一起訴訟，原告指控Twitch未經串流主同意、也沒有給予對應報酬，就把他們的直播內容拿去訓練AI。目前這起訴訟的更多細節，仍待進一步公開。

items.headline: 川普對加拿大車鋼加稅
items.context: 美國總統川普宣布，將把加拿大汽車、卡車與鋼鐵的關稅提高到50%，新稅率從2027年1月1日生效。這是美加貿易關係持續惡化的最新一步，川普同時在社群媒體上批評加拿大對美國農民「敲竹槓多年」。
items.thread_text: 美國總統川普宣布，加拿大進口的汽車、卡車、汽車零件與鋼鐵，關稅將調高到50%，新稅率從2027年1月1日開始實施。這是美加兩國貿易關係持續惡化的最新一步，川普同時在社群媒體上批評，加拿大對美國農民「敲竹槓多年」。

items.context: 美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）上週宣布加碼收購公債，想壓低殖利率，但效果不如預期。到上週五，10年期公債殖利率已回到宣布前的水準，30年期殖利率則貼近20多年來最高點。
items.thread_text: 美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）上週宣布，政府將加碼收購公債，希望藉此拉高債券價格、壓低殖利率——也就是政府舉債要付的利息。結果不如預期：宣布後殖利率一度下滑，但很快又彈回去。到上週五，10年期公債殖利率幾乎回到宣布前的水準，30年期殖利率則貼近20多年來的最高點。
items.threads_text: 美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）上週宣布，政府要加碼收購公債，目的是拉高債券價格、壓低殖利率——殖利率越低，代表政府舉債的利息負擔越輕。這項政策一開始看似奏效，公債殖利率短暫下滑，但很快又彈回原點。到上週五，10年期公債殖利率幾乎回到政策宣布前的水準，30年期公債殖利率甚至貼近20多年來的最高點。這場拉鋸也讓外界重新討論，在龐大財政赤字與市場信心動搖之下，美國公債作為全球避風港資產的地位，是否正在鬆動。

items.thread_text: 快時尚集團Shein即將在香港證券交易所掛牌，9月1日上市，這次設定的估值大約 270 億美元，比四年前私募市場高峰時逼近 1000 億美元的估值，大幅縮水。今年第一季，Shein出現 9900 萬美元虧損，公司的環境足跡也持續受到外界檢視。
items.threads_text: 快時尚集團Shein，靠著超低價策略打下一片市場版圖，這次卻不得不在香港上市時，大幅調低自己的估值。Shein將於9月1日在香港證券交易所掛牌，這次設定的估值大約 270 億美元，比四年前私募市場高峰時逼近 1000 億美元的估值，縮水超過七成。背後的原因並不難理解：今年第一季，Shein出現 9900 萬美元的虧損，同時也持續面臨外界對其環境足跡的檢視與批評。從近千億美元的估值，到如今打折上市，Shein這幾年的處境，某種程度上也是快時尚產業近年遭遇的縮影。

items.headline: 輝達伺服器違法轉賣中國起訴9人
items.context: 基隆地檢偵結一起非法出口案，起訴輝達（Nvidia）台灣經銷夥伴張姓經理，以及美超微公司台灣分公司林姓、王姓資深業務協理等9人。檢方指控，這些人涉嫌以不實文件申報出口，把搭載輝達高階晶片的AI伺服器，非法轉賣到中港澳地區。
items.thread_text: 基隆地方檢察署偵結一起非法出口案，起訴9人，其中包括輝達（Nvidia）台灣經銷事業部資深合作夥伴張姓經理，以及美超微公司台灣分公司林姓、王姓資深業務協理。檢方指控，這些人涉嫌以不實文件申報出口，把搭載輝達高階晶片的AI伺服器，非法轉賣到中國、香港與澳門。
items.threads_text: 基隆地方檢察署偵結一起非法出口案，起訴共9人，其中包括輝達（Nvidia）台灣經銷事業部資深合作夥伴張姓經理，以及美超微公司（Supermicro）台灣分公司林姓、王姓資深業務協理。檢方調查發現，這些人無視美國的出口管制措施，向美超微公司採購搭載輝達高階晶片的AI伺服器後，以不實文件申報出口，把伺服器非法轉賣到中國、香港與澳門地區。這起案件牽涉到美國近年針對高階AI晶片流向的出口管制規定，也反映出這類管制在台灣科技供應鏈中，正被越來越嚴格地執行。
items.voice_text: 台灣這邊有一則跟晶片有關的消息。（停頓一下）基隆地檢起訴了9個人，其中包括輝達在台灣的經銷合作夥伴，還有美超微公司台灣分公司的兩名資深業務協理。檢方說，這些人不理會美國的出口管制，買了搭載輝達高階晶片的AI伺服器之後，用假的申報文件，把伺服器偷偷轉賣到中國、香港跟澳門。這件事也跟台灣有關——牽涉到的，正是美國這幾年一直在緊盯的高階AI晶片出口管制。
